description:
Three expectation stores are append-only with no retraction path. Verified at
main 417c5b0b5:

    StructExpectationMap          src/compiler2/structdef.rs:103
      references / fields, both HashMap<ModuleId, Vec<..>>
      record_reference (:115) and record_field (:125) are contains-then-push
      no clear, no remove, no generation field

    ModuleInterface.expectations  src/compiler2/module_interface.rs:123
      record_expectation (:169) contains-then-push
      inherit_expectations_from (:176) blindly re-records every prior
        expectation with no staleness filter
      called from World::merge_module_interface_expectations (world.rs:753)

    ModuleReferenceExpectationMap module_interface.rs:90-107
      HashMap<ModuleId, Vec<..>>, record (:102) same shape, no removal

## Why it cannot fire today, by construction

`CodeMap::define` (code.rs:60) always mints `CodeId(self.slots.len() as u32)` and
pushes. `grep -rn "fn update_code|watch_mode|resubmit" src/compiler2/` returns
NOTHING. There is no in-place code-update primitive, so no edit can retract a
reference, and a stale expectation can never be consulted.

That makes this LATENT -- and it becomes live the moment the compiler stays
resident and recompiles on file change, which is the direction fz-kdt.4 (demand
cone) is also blocked on.

## The design question, which is what this ticket is for

Not settleable by running anything:

- Should retraction be generation-scoped (bump a generation on code redefinition,
  ignore expectations from older generations) or requester-revision-scoped?
- Should the three stores FOLD into one? They are three instances of the same
  idea -- "module M is expected to provide X, recorded by requester R" -- with
  three separate append-only vecs and three separate contains-then-push methods.
  Per [[feedback_fold_concordant_ideas]] that is worth answering before adding a
  retraction mechanism to each of them separately.

## Line drift in the old ticket

`record_expectation` is module_interface.rs:169 (was cited ~123-132, which is now
the `expectations` field). `merge_module_interface_expectations` is world.rs:753
(was ~1057-1064). What it calls "StructExpectationMap::record" is actually TWO
methods, `record_reference` and `record_field`.
title: Three expectation stores are append-only with no retraction, and are three instances of one idea
